thread:
sara: Following the recent partial-response incidents, here's a concise remediation plan focused on reconnects/timeouts. Need owners, short timeline, and measurable gates. Suggest owners: @kevin (runtime), @anya (observability/alerts), @tomas (SDK audit), @lina (customer comms). Agree?
tomas: Good call. I'll handle SDK audit. Will look for aggressive reconnect loops and gap between TCP close and reconnect.
kevin: I'll own runtime changes. Immediate actions: 1) add keepalive pings from server every 5s for streaming connections, 2) stop-the-world kv-cache eviction -> convert to incremental evict, 3) add serverirst-partial ACK to unblock clients that close early.
anya: I'll build dashboards and alerts. Proposed metrics/thresholds: p95_first_token_ms < 300ms, partial_response_rate < 0.3% over 10m, handshake_timeout_rate < 0.1% over 5m. If gates fail, rollback.
sara: Timeline proposal: triage + repro within 24h, patch PR in 48h, canary 3 days after PR merge, metrics gate 24h on canary before 50% rollout.
kevin: Reproducer: small python script hitting streaming endpoint with simulated flaky network (attached). Will instrument timestamps at: receive->kv_lookup->kv_evict->first_token_send. 
kevin: snippet of backoff config we'll add to runtime config (dev-friendly):
```
reconnect_policy:
  base_ms: 200
  max_ms: 5000
  factor: 2.0
  jitter: 0.3
```
kevin: Also adding server-side circuit breaker to avoid noisy neighbors causing global stalls. Per-tenant eviction window + non-blocking GC.
tomas: For SDKs I'll search for reconnect loops that re-open before TCP FIN processed. Also check exponential backoff implementations -- some envs had linear ramps. I'll open RD-10113 for cross-client compatibility.
anya: Dashboards I'll add: partial_response_rate by deployment (hosted/dedicated/private), first_token_latency histogram, keepalive_missed_count, active_streams_by_node. Will wire alerts to pager if >0.5% partials for 10m on prod.
sara: Ops plan: canary on hosted cluster first, then dedicated pool; we need a rollback play if partials increase. ops-bot can you schedule?
ops-bot: Canary deploy RD-runtime v1.22.4 to cluster canary-3 at 2026-03-11T02:00Z. Rollback window: 2h after deploy if partial_response_rate rises >0.1% absolute.
kevin: We'll make keepalive and ACK features toggleable via config flags so canary can test without forcing client upgrades. Default: keepalive=on for runtime, ack=off for older clients.
marc: Customer comms: Lina handle with Tomas's SDK notes. We'll include timeline and mitigation steps in customer emails.
lina: will draft. Need list of affected customers and deployment IDs.
kevin: Found correlated logs: nodes a1,a3 had kv-evict spikes at the same time as partial responses. Putting sample trace here: "kv_evict start=1616161616.123 end=1616161616.987 blocked_by_gc=true"
anya: Added runbook stub: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/stream-partial-resp>. Will include playbook to roll back to previous runtime and how to interpret metrics.
sara: Action items: RD-10110 (kevin) runtime fixes (keepalive + incremental eviction + circuit breaker), RD-10111 (anya) dashboards/alerts + runbook, RD-10112 (tomas) SDK audit + compatibility notes, RD-10113 (lina) customer comms + impacted list. Set ETA: triage 24h, PRs 48h, canary within 5 days.
incident-bot: Recorded action items: RD-10110 (owner: kevin), RD-10111 (owner: anya), RD-10112 (owner: tomas), RD-10113 (owner: lina).
sara: Please post daily 1-2 line status updates in this thread until RD-10110/11/12/13 are closed. We'll have a short sync after canary metrics are in.
kevin: opened RD-10110 and pushed initial instrumented build to internal bucket. Reproducer script link: <https://storage.redwood.internal/incident/1865501123/repro.py>.
tomas: started SDK audit, found one JS client with 100ms reconnect loop when network jitter present. Adding mitigation and will propose a patch to SDK RD-10112.
anya: dashboards mostly wired, alert thresholds in PR for runbook review.
marc: thanks all. tagging @incident-bot to add these to the postmortem follow-up checklist.
incident-bot: Postmortem follow-up updated. Next review in 3 days or when canary completes.
